title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, talk to seniors and clients in the right register, handle meetings and deadlines, ask for leave and read office emails and notices.
intro:
Office Marathi in Pune and Mumbai is a constant switch: **तू** and English-heavy banter with the colleague you have chai with (**कामाचा खूप लोड आहे यार**), **तुम्ही** and **सर / मॅडम** with your boss, and a stiff written register in emails and notices (**कृपया नोंद घ्यावी** 'please note').

This unit gives you all three. The grammar covers the **formal register** — very formal **आपण** 'you', talking about seniors in the plural, the written **-आवे** request form — and the ways Marathi says 'it was decided' or 'the meeting has been cancelled': the everyday **ठरलं / रद्द झाली**, and the official **रद्द करण्यात आली** you'll read in every HR email.

grammar.title: Formal register: आपण, सर / मॅडम, and the written -आवे
grammar.body:
At work in Maharashtra you move between three registers in the same hour: **तू** with the colleague you have lunch with, **तुम्ही** with most people, and a **formal** register with senior people, clients and in writing.

**Speaking formally**
- Use **तुम्ही** with anyone senior. The very formal **आपण** 'you' takes exactly the same verb forms: आपण कधी **आलात**? 'when did you arrive?', आपण उपलब्ध **असाल** का? 'would you be available?'. Its possessive is **आपला / आपली / आपलं**: आपलं नाव? 'your name, please?'. Remember आपण is also inclusive 'we' (आपण नंतर चर्चा करू 'let's discuss it later') — context decides.
- Talk **about** seniors in the plural: साहेब **आले आहेत**, मॅडम मीटिंगमध्ये **आहेत**, **त्यांनी** सांगितलं. Using the singular (तो आला) for your boss sounds rude.
- Address: **सर / मॅडम** in offices, even to people your age at first; **-साहेब** after a surname (पाटीलसाहेब); **-ताई / -दादा** after a first name for friendly respect (स्नेहाताई).
- Ask, don't tell: **…शकतो का?**, **…मिळेल का?**, **-आल का?** (Unit 18).

**Writing formally: the -आवे form**
Emails, notices and messages to a boss use stem + **आवे** — the polite impersonal 'one should', with no 'you' at all: **कळवावे** 'kindly let us know', **यावे** 'please come', **नोंद घ्यावी** 'please note'. Like Unit 15's -आवं लागणे, it agrees with an object: रिपोर्ट (m) पाठवा**वा**, रजा (f) मंजूर करा**वी**. Out loud this sounds stiff; in speech say **कळवा** or **कळवाल का?**.

**The trap:** never mix तू forms into a formal sentence (आपण येशील? ✗ → आपण याल का? ✓). And English loans are fine in formal speech (मीटिंग, रिपोर्ट, डेडलाइन): what makes Marathi formal is the pronouns and verb forms, not Sanskrit words.

grammar.title: 'It was decided': ठरलं, रद्द झाली, रद्द करण्यात आली
grammar.body:
English uses the passive constantly ('the meeting was cancelled', 'it was decided'). Marathi has three ways to say this, from everyday to official.

**1. The intransitive partner (everyday speech)**
Many Marathi verbs come in pairs: a transitive one that needs a doer and an intransitive one where things just happen. ठरवणे 'decide' / **ठरणे** 'get decided'; रद्द करणे / **रद्द होणे**; पूर्ण करणे / **पूर्ण होणे**; सुरू करणे / सुरू होणे; बंद करणे / बंद होणे. So: असं **ठरलं** की… 'it was decided that…', मीटिंग रद्द **झाली** 'the meeting got cancelled', काम पूर्ण **झालं** 'the work is done'. English loans work the same way: मीटिंग पोस्टपोन **झाली**, रजा अप्रूव्ह **झाली**. This is what you will say 99% of the time.

**2. Past participle + जाणे (the true passive)**
The past form of the verb, agreeing with the object, + जाणे: इथे मराठी बोलली **जाते** 'Marathi is spoken here', हा प्रश्न नेहमी विचारला **जातो** 'this question always gets asked'. Used for general facts and rules.

**3. -ण्यात आलं (official)**
The verbal noun in **-ण्यात** + **आला / आली / आलं / आले**, agreeing with the thing done: निर्णय घे**ण्यात आला** 'a decision has been taken', मीटिंग रद्द कर**ण्यात आली** 'the meeting has been cancelled', ऑफिस बंद ठेव**ण्यात येईल** 'the office will remain closed'. This is the voice of circulars, HR emails, government notices and the news. You'll read it far more than you say it.

**The trap:** 'it was decided' is **ठरलं** (no doer, no ने), not ठरवलं — ठरवलं needs someone: साहेबांनी ठरवलं 'the boss decided'.

culture:
Office Marathi is heavily mixed with English — **मीटिंग पोस्टपोन झाली**, **डेडलाइन मिस झाली**, **कॉलवर आहे** — and nobody finds that odd; what changes with the person is the pronoun and the verb ending. Juniors call seniors **सर / मॅडम** (or **अजय सर**, **स्नेहा मॅडम**), never a bare first name; a senior may well call you **तू**. Among peers, **तू** comes quickly, usually over the tea break: in Hinjewadi or Baner the **टपरी** (roadside tea stall) outside the IT park is where the real office conversation happens.

In Mumbai offices you'll hear as much Hindi and English as Marathi, but in Pune, and in any **सरकारी कार्यालय** (government office) across the state, Marathi is the default. Government notices, bank letters and Marathi newspapers are written in the formal register with **-ण्यात आले** and **-आवे**: *सर्व कर्मचाऱ्यांनी नोंद घ्यावी* 'all staff please note'. You don't need to speak like that, but you'll need to read it.

Leave is usually asked for in person first and then 'put on mail' (**मेलवर टाका**). Family functions — a sister's **साखरपुडा** (engagement), a wedding in the native village (**गावी लग्न आहे**) — are accepted reasons everywhere.

tip.title: तू or तुम्ही at work?
tip.body:
- Colleagues your age, once you know them: **तू** (चहाला येतोस का?).
- Seniors, clients, anyone you've just met: **तुम्ही** — and **सर / मॅडम**.
- Talk *about* a senior in the plural: बॉस **आले**, **त्यांनी** विचारलं.
- English work words are normal: ब्रेक, टीम, अपडेट.

tip.title: Formal: आपण, सर, and the plural
tip.body:
- Very formal 'you' is **आपण**, with the तुम्ही verb forms: आपण कधी **आलात**? Its possessive is **आपला / आपली / आपलं**.

- Ask, don't tell: **…शकतो का?**, **…मिळेल का?**, **-आल का?**
- Never mix in तू forms.

tip.title: It was decided: ठरलं, रद्द झाली
tip.body:
- In speech, use the **intransitive** partner: ठरवणे → **ठरलं**, रद्द करणे → रद्द **झाली**, पूर्ण करणे → पूर्ण **झालं**.
- With English loans: पोस्टपोन **झाली**, अप्रूव्ह **झालं**.
- Notices use **-ण्यात आलं**: निर्णय घे**ण्यात आला**.
- No ने: 'it was decided' is ठरलं, not ठरवलं.

tip.title: Office writing: कळवावे, करण्यात आलं
tip.body:
- Emails and notices use stem + **आवे** for 'please': **कळवावे** 'kindly let me know', **नोंद घ्यावी** 'please note'. It agrees with an object: रिपोर्ट पाठवा**वा**.
- Announcements use **-ण्यात आलं** for 'has been done': मीटिंग रद्द कर**ण्यात आली**.
- Out loud you'd just say **कळवा**, **मीटिंग रद्द झाली**.

tip.title: Asking for time off
tip.body:
- Ask with **मिळेल का?**: मला शुक्रवारची रजा **मिळेल का?**
- Give the reason briefly: गावी लग्न आहे, मला बरं वाटत नाही.
- Leave is **रजा** (f): रजा **घेणे**, रजे**वर** असणे, रजा **मंजूर** होणे.
- 'Half day' and 'sick leave' are said in English.

sentences.roman: hī mājhī dzabābdārī āhe, mī baghto.
sentences.en: This is my responsibility, I'll handle it. (man)
The pay rise was good this year.

sentences.native: त्याने काल राजीनामा दिला आणि सगळ्यांना धक्का बसला.
sentences.roman: tyāne kāl rādzīnāmā dilā āṇi sagḷyānnā dhakkā baslā.
sentences.en: He resigned yesterday and everyone was shocked.
I've got five years' experience.
Why are you resigning?

sentences.native: नवीन कंपनीत पगार जास्त आहे आणि काम पण चांगलं आहे.
sentences.roman: navīn kampanīt pagār dzāst āhe āṇi kām paṇ tsāṅglaṃ āhe.
sentences.en: At the new company the pay is better and the work is good too.
At the interview they asked about my experience.
I'll have to give a month's notice.

sentences.native: पगारवाढ नाही, तर मी पण राजीनामा देणार!
sentences.roman: pagārvāḍh nāhī, tar mī paṇ rādzīnāmā deṇār!
sentences.en: No raise? Then I'm resigning too!
This is a first for me.
